Rising river levels today may lead to flooding.
Flooding is possible on Tuesday 17 November .
Areas most at risk include low lying areas in Tetbury, Badminton, Brook End at Luckington, Corsham, Lacock and the road at Reybridge.
Flooding is forecast to affect locations near the Bristol Avon, Tetbury Avon, Sherston Avon, Dauntsey Brook, with low lying land and roads expected to be most affected, particularly around low lying areas in Tetbury, Badminton, Brook End at Luckington, Corsham, Lacock and the road at Reybridge.
Flooding is possible throughout Tuesday as river levels rise due to the overnight rainfall.
We are monitoring rainfall and river levels .
Avoid low lying roads near rivers, which may be flooded.  
This message will be updated by 5:00PM on Tuesday 17 November or as the situation changes.

Higher than normal tides tomorrow morning may lead to flooding. 
Flooding is possible from 03:14AM to 07:14AM on 17/11/26. 
The highest tide level is expected to be at Christchurch Harbour and tidal stretches of the Lower Stour and Avon at 05:14AM on 17/11/2026 with a level of 1.24 mAODN and a South Westerly force 7 wind. Our threshold for issuing the Flood Alert for Christchurch Harbour is 1.20 mAODN so we anticipate only a small rise above this level. 
We are closely monitoring the situation .Start acting on your flood plan if you have one. 
Avoid beaches and coastal promenades, which may be flooded. Avoid coastal roads and low lying roads near rivers, which may be flooded. 
This message will be updated by 12:00PM on Tuesday 17 November or as the situation changes.

items.message:
High river levels are expected to cause flooding this morning. 
Flooding is expected from the morning of Tuesday 17 November . 
Areas most at risk are properties at Prince William Way, Prince William Road, Jubilee Drive, Monarch Way, Waldron Court, Belton Road West Extension, Lisle Street and Derby Road near Burleigh Brook. If levels continue to rise, properties at Bottleacre Lane, Belton Road near Bottleacre Lane, Staveley Court, Meadow Avenue, Waterside Close and surrounding areas are at risk. Light rainfall is forecast over the next 6 hours. River levels at Lisle Street Gauge are rising rapidly due to the nature of the catchment. 
We are closely monitoring the situation . 
Move family, pets and cars to safety and turn off gas, electricity and water if it is safe to do so. & start acting on your flood plan, if you have one. 
This message will be updated by 5:00PM on Tuesday 17 November or as the situation changes.
